headline: Earnings week recap: 24 of 26 beat on EPS, AppLovin +44%, Marathon Petroleum −13%, 10 beat and still fell; CoreWeave, Cisco and Applied Materials report in the week ahead
top_call: This week 24 of 26 big companies beat Wall Street on earnings, and the market still made 10 of them pay. AppLovin ripped about 44%, Marathon Petroleum sank about 13%, and the rest landed somewhere between 'nice quarter' and 'nice quarter, sell it.' Every explainer is linked below, biggest names first, plus who reports in the week ahead: CoreWeave Tuesday, Cisco and Applied Materials Thursday.
lead_title: 24 of 26 beat earnings this week, and 10 still fell
subject: The Daily Five — Sun Nov 8: 24 of 26 beat earnings, 10 still fell; AppLovin +44%
backdrop: Friday's bounce: the S&P 500 rose 0.3% and the Nasdaq gained 1.1% as Nvidia climbed 2.8% after two days of AI-led selling, while the Dow slipped 237 points (0.5%). The S&P still lost 2.7% on the week, its worst week since the April 2025 tariff shock, per AP.
on_deck_sub: The big reports Nov 9–12 and what Wall Street expects (EPS estimates per Yahoo Finance)

ai.headline: Anthropic is pushing ahead with a pre-Thanksgiving IPO anyway: $80–100 billion raise at a $1.25–1.75 trillion valuation, below the $2 trillion some backers dreamed of, per investors cited by the FT
ai.why: The AI rout just gave the biggest IPO of the year a haircut, and they're showing up to the barber anyway. OpenAI also trimmed its private round to $1.25 trillion. A soft print here is a mood ring for every AI stock.

ai.headline: The U.S. cleared a Chinese firm with an empty Beijing office, and owners tied to a blacklisted private-equity firm, to buy Nvidia H200 chips, per a New York Times investigation
ai.why: Export controls, but make it honor system. Expect Washington to tighten the screws, which is a headline risk for Nvidia ahead of its Nov 17 report.

ai.headline: Meta's chief strategy officer and former CFO Dave Wehner is leaving to become CFO of Fireworks, a $17.5 billion AI inference startup reportedly in talks to raise at $30–40 billion
ai.why: When Meta's old money guy picks the picks-and-shovels startup, that's a tell about where he thinks the AI cash lands: running the models, not just building them.
